purpose.description: Construct hidden-state counterexamples showing that identical external observations can correspond to different internal causal states and future target values.
purpose.role: Generalize interface non-identifiability from finite observation ambiguity to latent-state ambiguity.
not_used_for: claiming hidden states are always unrecoverable
proving internal access is always required

system_class.description: Systems containing latent internal states not directly exposed by the declared interface.

observation_operator.definition: Maps full system state and dynamics to externally available observations.

target_functional.definition: Future target dependent on hidden-state evolution.

hidden_state_pairs.description: Systems have identical observable history but different hidden memory states.
Systems exhibit identical adaptation traces but differ in future update capability.
Multiple latent states map to the same observable state.

equivalence_class_analysis.interpretation: The observation map collapses latent distinctions that remain relevant to the target.

connection_to_factorization.failure_reason: No function of observations alone can assign a unique target value to the hidden-state equivalence class.
connection_to_factorization.result: Factorization fails over the declared hidden-state class.

established: the tested external interface cannot identify hidden-state-dependent targets
not_established: all hidden states require direct measurement
latent variables are impossible to infer

decision.meaning: The declared external interface is insufficient when the target depends on latent state distinctions.

notes: Hidden-state failure is an interface limitation, not a statement about the existence of latent information.
The correct question remains whether the target factors through the chosen interface.
A sufficient interface may expose latent consequences without directly exposing latent variables.
